title: Harness Engineering: Engineering Principles That Make AI Agents Truly Useful
html:
Agent = Model + Harness

Understanding Harness Engineering starts with a definition:

Agent = Model + Harness

The model is the source of intelligence; the harness is the system that makes that intelligence useful. The converse also holds: if a component is not the model itself, it is part of the harness.

A bare model is not an agent. It takes text, images, and audio as input and outputs text. That is all. Out of the box, it cannot maintain persistent state across sessions, execute code, access real-time knowledge, or set up an environment to get work done. The harness builds these capabilities around the model.

A harness includes:

  • System Prompts: Inject initial instructions and context
  • Tools, Skills, MCPs: Give the model callable capability interfaces
  • Infrastructure: Execution environments such as filesystems, sandboxes, and browsers
  • Orchestration logic: Subagent scheduling, task dispatch, and model routing
  • Hooks / Middleware: Deterministic execution layers for checkpoints, linting, compaction, and more

Deriving Harness Structure from Model Limitations

Every harness component can be derived by asking, "What do we want the agent to do that a bare model cannot?"

The Filesystem: The Most Basic Harness Primitive

A model can directly manipulate only information in its current context window. Before filesystems, providing data meant pasting content directly into the conversation, which is completely impractical for autonomous agents.

The filesystem is the harness's central primitive because it unlocks a range of higher-level capabilities:

  • Agents gain a workspace where they can read code, data, and documents
  • Intermediate artifacts can be written and read incrementally, without keeping everything in context
  • Task state can persist across sessions
  • Multiple agents or people can collaborate through shared files; the filesystem is a natural collaboration interface
  • With Git, agents can track changes, roll back mistakes, and run parallel experiments

Bash + Code Execution: A General-Purpose Tool

Today's mainstream agent execution pattern is the ReAct loop: model reasoning → tool call → observe results → reason again. But a harness can only execute tools whose logic it already implements. Designing a tool for every possible operation is extremely expensive and inflexible.

Giving an agent a Bash tool is a better solution: the model can design the tools it needs by writing code, rather than being confined to a fixed set of preconfigured tools. Code execution has become the default general-purpose strategy for autonomous problem solving.

Sandboxes: Safe Execution Environments

Once you have filesystem access and code execution, you still need somewhere to run them. Executing agent-generated code locally poses security risks, and a single local environment cannot support large numbers of concurrent agent tasks.

Sandboxes let agents run code, inspect files, and install dependencies in isolation. The harness decides where an agent runs, what it can access, and which commands it can execute. These are all harness-layer design decisions; a model cannot configure its own execution environment.

Sandboxes also enable scale: execution environments can be created on demand, distributed in parallel, and destroyed after tasks finish.

Memory and Search: Overcoming Knowledge Limitations

A model's knowledge is locked in its training weights; information outside its context is invisible to it. The solution is context injection.

The filesystem comes into play again here. Memory-file standards such as AGENTS.md let agents accumulate and pass knowledge between sessions: an agent writes what it learned in the current session to a file, and the harness injects that file into context at the start of the next session, creating a form of continuous learning.

For real-time knowledge after the training cutoff, Web Search and MCP tools such as Context7 give agents access to the latest library versions, current data, and other information that did not exist during training.

Two Core Engineering Challenges

Context Rot

Agent performance should not degrade the longer it works, but in practice it does. This phenomenon is called Context Rot: as the context window fills, the model's reasoning quality and task-completion ability steadily decline.

A harness needs dedicated mechanisms to combat context rot:

Compaction: As the context window approaches its limit, the harness must strategically summarize and offload existing context so the agent can keep working instead of being interrupted by an API error.

Tool-output truncation: Large tool responses can fill the context window, even though useful information often appears only at the beginning and end. The harness retains the first and last tokens, offloads the full output to the filesystem, and reads it on demand when needed.

Progressive disclosure of Skills: Loading every tool and MCP server into context at once consumes many tokens before the agent even starts. Skills address this through progressive disclosure: relevant Skill metadata is injected into context only when needed.

These mechanisms share one principle: Context is a scarce resource, and the harness is the execution layer for context engineering.

Long-Horizon Execution

Enabling agents to autonomously complete complex tasks over extended periods is one of the central challenges in agent engineering today. Bare models face problems such as premature termination, inability to decompose complex problems, and inconsistent behavior across multiple context windows.

Ralph Loop: A harness pattern that intercepts a model's attempts to exit through a hook, reinjects the original task objective into a fresh context window, and forces the agent to keep progressing until completion criteria are met. The filesystem makes this possible: each iteration starts with clean context but reads the previous state from disk.

Planning and self-verification: Through prompt injection and filesystem support, the harness helps agents break goals into steps and verify each step's output by running tests, inspecting logs, and comparing expected results. Test results and errors return to the model as feedback, forming a self-correction loop.

Design by Contract: The Harness's Constraint Layer

Beyond supplying capabilities—the tools and environments a model needs—a harness also needs a constraint layer to manage the model's nondeterministic behavior.

Every LLM output is the result of probabilistic sampling, and behavior is extremely sensitive to context. More importantly, prompt constraints are soft in engineering terms:

  • Attention dilution: As conversation turns accumulate, constraints in the system prompt carry progressively less weight in the overall context
  • Physical truncation: When the context window fills, the earliest content—usually constraint rules—is discarded first
  • No execution semantics: Natural-language instructions constrain a model probabilistically, not through enforcement

The harness's constraint layer is best understood through Design by Contract:

Preconditions: Before the model performs a high-impact operation, the harness inserts a mandatory checkpoint. The model must produce a structured execution intent—goal, scope, side effects, and verification method—which external logic, rather than the model itself, validates before allowing execution. The crucial point is that validation happens outside the model.

Postconditions: After an operation, the harness requires verification evidence from external systems: unit-test results, runtime logs, API responses, and filesystem diffs. This evidence becomes the model's next input, switching it from self-assessment to evidence-driven operation.

Invariants: Maintain an external state document recording task goals, completed work and supporting evidence, technical decisions and their reasons, and unresolved issues. The model's internal context may disappear at any time, but this document remains the task's single source of truth, allowing any session to restore its state.

Harness Architecture

Translating these components into a system design:

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       Harness Layer                       │
│                                                           │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌───────────────┐  ┌────────────────┐  │
│  │  State Store │  │ Checkpoint    │  │   Evaluator    │  │
│  │  (Spec /     │  │ Gate          │  │  (证据收集 /   │  │
│  │   Handoff)   │  │ (前置断言)    │  │   后置断言)    │  │
│  └──────┬───────┘  └──────┬────────┘  └───────┬────────┘  │
│         │                 │                   │            │
│  ┌──────┴─────────────────┴───────────────────┴────────┐  │
│  │   Orchestration Logic + Hooks / Middleware           │  │
│  │   (Ralph Loop / Compaction / Tool Output Offload)   │  │
│  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└──────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────────┘
                           │
              ┌────────────▼────────────┐
              │        LLM Core          │
              │  Context Assembly →      │
              │  Inference → Action      │
              └────────────┬────────────┘
                           │
          ┌────────────────┴────────────────┐
          ▼                                 ▼
┌──────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
│  Tools / Skills  │             │  Execution Sandbox   │
│  MCPs / APIs     │             │  Filesystem / Git    │
└──────────────────┘             └──────────────────────┘

Capability Design: Narrowing the Model's Decision Space

The harness addresses execution boundaries; capability design addresses capability boundaries.

Exposing tools at too fine a granularity creates two problems: the huge space of tool combinations makes decisions hard to validate, and dependencies and side effects between tools remain unencapsulated, so a mistake at any step can cascade.

A better approach is to package tools into capabilities with clear business semantics:

# 暴露基础工具：Model 需要自己组合和判断副作用
tools = [read_file, write_file, run_sql, call_api, ...]

# 封装成 Capability：Model 只需选择业务操作
capabilities = [
    update_user_profile,    # 内部封装校验、写库、缓存失效
    run_regression_suite,   # 内部封装环境准备、执行、结果收集
    deploy_to_staging,      # 内部封装构建、推送、健康检查
]

Each capability contains its own validator. The model's unit of decision changes from "which API should I call, with what parameters?" to "which business operation should I choose?" A smaller decision space is easier to validate and less likely to go out of control.

Recognizing Poor Harness Design

Before discussing how to build a harness properly, we must distinguish two fundamentally different problems: having no harness at all, and having a poor-quality harness. They manifest differently and require entirely different remedies.

No Harness at All

These designs share one feature: there are no enforced constraints outside the model, and all control relies on the model's internal "self-restraint."

The soft-constraint trap: Piling rules and prohibitions into the system prompt and expecting the model to follow them voluntarily. This effectively hands control of execution boundaries to the probabilistic engine itself. The longer the rules, the more likely they are to be diluted or forgotten during long workflows, with no external mechanism to guarantee their enforcement at any moment.

Missing tool boundaries: Exposing many fine-grained tools without defining usage boundaries leaves tool selection entirely to the model's reasoning. This is more than a capability-design problem: it is a loss of control at the harness layer, with no mechanism to intervene before a dangerous tool call.

Neither case constitutes a harness, because the control plane is not outside the model.

A Harness Exists, but Its Quality Is Poor

These designs have external control flow, but their control methods introduce new problems.

Bare retry loops: On detecting an error, simply feed the error back into the model's context and let it retry indefinitely. This is external control, but it does not realign goals and boundaries before retrying. In such a loop, the model converges toward whatever it thinks will eliminate the error, rather than the correct solution; fixing a syntax error may come at the cost of deleting an entire module. Effective retries require the model to restate the current objective and confirm the repair scope before each iteration, rather than continuing unchecked.

Excessive up-front documentation: Forcing the model to produce extensive design documents before taking any action, making documentation a prerequisite for execution. This is a form of state management, but the wrong granularity or timing has two costs: many tokens are spent generating documents, and documents become an unmaintainable burden once they diverge from execution. State management should provide a lightweight source of truth that stays synchronized, rather than heavyweight one-off documentation.

The distinction matters: the first problem calls for introducing a harness; the second calls for improving its design. Conflating them leads to trying to solve "no external constraints" by "adding more documentation," or evading "overly crude control" by "removing control entirely."

Managing Goal Hierarchies in Long Tasks

In long-horizon execution, beyond Ralph Loops and planning mechanisms, there is an easily overlooked runtime problem: models tend to bypass the current phase's specific objective and advance directly toward their interpretation of the overall goal.

The behavior looks busy, but each step tries to solve everything at once instead of progressing through decomposed steps. The longer the workflow, the further execution drifts from the plan.

An effective harness must maintain three levels of goals at runtime and keep them separate:

Overall goal: The completion criteria for the entire task or current major stage. This is an anchor that does not change with the outcome of an individual execution round.

Phase goal: The scope of problems that may be addressed over the next several conversation turns. Until a phase ends, the model must not bring the next phase's work into the current scope.

Current-round action goal: The number and boundaries of operations allowed in a single execution round, usually limited to one to three concrete actions.

The key constraint across these levels is: completing a phase does not mean completing the overall goal. Once a phase has converged, the harness must explicitly communicate that conclusion to the model, rather than letting it decide on its own whether to advance to the next phase.

Redefining Goals at Runtime

The goal hierarchy is not set once at the start and then frozen. When external evidence during execution—test failures, log anomalies, or API errors—conflicts with the current phase goal, that goal must be redefined.

This redefinition does not reject the plan; it is the normal mechanism by which the harness responds to real feedback. A typical example: the phase was meant to "complete feature X," but runtime logs reveal a systemic issue in a dependency chain. The phase goal should narrow to "first identify the root cause of the chain failure." Once that issue is resolved and accepted, work on the original phase goal can resume.

The harness supplies the external evidence that triggers redefinition and then forces the model to acknowledge the new phase boundaries, preventing it from immediately drifting back toward the overall goal.

Harness Control Points Within an Execution Round

Understanding harness architecture is one thing; understanding how it manifests in actual execution is another. In a complete execution round, harness control logic acts at the following key points.

Point One: Align on Goals Before Any Implementation

At the start of a task, the harness's first control point is to have the model restate its understanding rather than execute immediately: what it sees as the overall goal, the current phase's main focus, and the boundaries and open questions.

This step explicitly extracts the model's intent, exposing misunderstandings so they can be corrected before any code is written. Skip it, and faster subsequent execution only makes drift harder to notice.

Point Two: A Minimal Spec Locks the Round's Scope

After goal alignment, the model does not proceed straight to implementation. It first produces a lightweight execution spec: the current round's goal, scope boundaries, explicitly excluded work, and verification method.

The spec's central purpose is to prevent the model from smuggling higher-level goals into the current round. Without explicit boundaries, execution naturally expands toward the overall goal, turning a round intended only for A into simultaneous work on A, B, and C. The spec is the contract for this round; only what it contains may be executed.

Point Three: A Pre-execution Checkpoint

Before the model makes any actual change, the harness inserts a mandatory checkpoint: the model must explain in its own words its current understanding, concrete next actions, expected side effects, and how completion will be verified. Execution begins only after a person or rules engine confirms this output.

A checkpoint is not a formality; it is the final external validation of execution intent. If the model cannot articulate its plan clearly here, it usually has not formed a stable execution plan. Letting it proceed simply postpones the problem until execution.

Point Four: Acceptance Based on External Evidence

After execution, the harness refuses to accept the model's self-assessment as a completion signal. Acceptance rests on only three categories: test results; runtime logs and observed workflow behavior; and direct evidence from a test environment or manual verification.

This transfers authority over the completion judgment from the model to external systems. Models have a strong tendency to declare success after a task, but that tendency reflects generation probabilities, not whether the result is correct. External evidence is the only reliable acceptance criterion.

Acceptance must also explicitly distinguish two levels: whether the current phase goal is complete, and whether the overall goal is complete. These questions must be answered separately; the former cannot stand in for the latter.

Point Five: Runtime Course Correction

When surprises arise during execution—logged errors, API anomalies, or failed tests—the harness's runtime correction mechanism intervenes.

The key is to narrow the current round's scope before continuing the original plan. If logs reveal a systemic problem in a workflow, the round's goal narrows from "complete feature X" to "identify the root cause of the workflow problem." Only after that cause is demonstrably resolved does work on the original goal resume.

The most important point is that models naturally tend to "fix a few other things while they are at it" when receiving error feedback. The harness must keep repairs within the current minimal goal, rather than allowing expansion into other problems before the present repair is complete.

After correction, acceptance must again rely on external evidence—whether this minimal goal was actually completed—not the model's subjective judgment.

Future Directions for Harness Engineering

Harness Engineering is actively evolving. Several directions deserve attention:

Coevolution of model training and harness design: Current agent products already incorporate the harness into training. Models are post-trained through interaction with the harness, gradually acquiring stronger native abilities in filesystem operations, Bash execution, task planning, and parallel subagent work. As this loop continues, a model becomes stronger within the harness it was trained on, but can also overfit its details: changing tool-calling logic may reduce performance. Harness design is therefore an important variable in agent capability.

Dynamic harness assembly: Most harnesses today are statically preconfigured, with tools and context determined before a task begins. The future direction is to assemble exactly the tools and context needed for the current task on demand, rather than preload everything that might be used.

Agents analyzing harness failures: Let agents analyze their own execution traces, identify failure patterns at the harness layer, and suggest improvements, enabling the harness to optimize itself.

When to Introduce a Harness

Introducing a harness has an engineering cost. Use the following framework to assess where it applies:

ScenarioRequired harness components
Single call, stateless, repeatable taskAlmost none
Operations with side effects (database writes, API calls, file changes)Execution gates (preconditions)
Ongoing tasks across sessionsState Store + invariants
Evidence-based acceptance rather than trusting model self-assessmentEvaluator (postconditions)
Extended autonomous executionRalph Loop + planning + self-verification
Collaboration among multiple agents or peopleFilesystem as a shared collaboration layer
Complete enterprise deliveryAll of the above

The longer the workflow, the greater the side effects, and the more participants involved, the more valuable the harness becomes.

Summary

Harness Engineering is an engineering approach to building systems around model intelligence. The model handles reasoning and decisions; the harness enables that intelligence to work reliably, verifiably, and sustainably in real engineering environments.

Its core components are derived from two directions: model limitations imply the capabilities that must be supplied—filesystems, code execution, sandboxes, and memory—while engineering reliability requirements imply the necessary constraints—preconditions, postconditions, and invariants.

Prompt Engineering determines what a model can generate in a given context; Harness Engineering determines under what conditions those outputs are accepted or rejected, and how task state is saved and restored across sessions. They address problems at different layers.

 

References:From Toy to Productivity: Explaining AI Agent Harness Engineering Through a Real Project

https://www.langchain.com/blog/the-anatomy-of-an-agent-harness

Starting the Project

Step 1: Clone the Repository

git clone https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent.git

Step 2: Enter the Project Directory

cd /Users/YolieDeng/Code/hermes-agent

Step 3: Create and Activate a Virtual Environment

uv venv
source .venv/bin/activate

Step 4: Install Project Dependencies

    uv sync

Step 5: Configure the .env File

 cp .env.example .env 
 # 编辑 .env，填入你的 API 密钥

Step 5: Select a Model and Launch Directly

hermes doctor 
# 选择适合的模型
hermes model
hermes

title: Hermes Agent Tutorial (2): System Architecture and Design
html:
Hermes Agent: System Architecture and Design

Intended audience: Developers seeking a systematic understanding of Hermes Agent's architecture and design philosophy
Prerequisites: Familiarity with AI agents and LLMs (large language models)
Documentation: https://github.com/Eva-Dengyh/AI-Fullstack-Notes

Contents

  • Chapter 1: What Is Hermes?
  • Chapter 2: Why Has Hermes Taken Off?
  • Chapter 3: System Architecture Overview
  • Chapter 4: Core Module Design
  • Chapter 5: The Tool System—Registry Pattern
  • Chapter 6: The Messaging Gateway—Adapter Pattern
  • Chapter 7: The AI Loop—ReAct Pattern
  • Chapter 8: Prompt Construction—Layered Assembly
  • Chapter 9: Memory and Skills
  • Chapter 10: Model Abstraction—Provider Pattern
  • Chapter 11: What Makes the Architecture Good?
  • Chapter 12: Popular Features Explained

Chapter 1: What Is Hermes?

A one-sentence definition:

Hermes Agent is a self-improving AI agent framework built by Nous Research. It is one of the most complete open-source agent solutions available, integrating multiplatform access, persistent memory, evolving skills, and parallel subagent execution.

What you can do with it:

在终端里跟它聊天                    ✅
在 Telegram 里跟它聊天              ✅
在 Discord 里跟它聊天               ✅
在微信里跟它聊天                    ✅
让它帮你读写文件、搜索网页、跑代码     ✅
让它记住你说过的重要事情              ✅
让它从错误里学习，下次做得更好         ✅
设置定时任务让它自动执行              ✅
同时做多件独立的事（子Agent）         ✅
切换到任何一个 LLM 模型              ✅
把它部署在云端，省电省钱              ✅

Why "Hermes"?

Hermes, the messenger god of Greek mythology, was the fastest and best informed. The name reflects two core agent capabilities: delivering messages and responding quickly.

Chapter 2: Why Has Hermes Taken Off?

2.1 The AI Agent Market in 2024–2025

Most AI agent products have the following pain points:

Competitor LimitationHermes's Solution
Locked to one model, such as Claude or GPTSwitch to any model with one configuration change, without changing code
Locked to one platform, such as Telegram or DiscordOne gateway connects all major chat platforms
Every conversation starts from scratch, with no memory of previous eventsPersistent memory and Skills accumulate across sessions
Fixed functionality with no way to add capabilities60+ built-in tools plus the MCP extension protocol
Resource consumption and high always-on operating costsCloud hibernation on Daytona or Modal, with near-zero idle costs
Closed source and not customizableFully open source under the MIT license

2.2 Hermes's Core Differentiators

你想要的                        Hermes 做到的
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
换模型（Claude → GPT → 开源模型）    ✅ 一个 /model 命令，秒级切换
换平台（终端 → Telegram → 微信）     ✅ 一个 gateway，配置即接
Agent 记住重要信息                  ✅ 跨会话持久记忆
Agent 学会新技能                   ✅ Skills 系统，经验可复用
后台自动跑任务                      ✅ Cron 定时任务，自然语言配置
同时做多件事                       ✅ 子 Agent 并行执行
省成本（不用时休眠）                ✅ Daytona/Modal 云端休眠，近零费用
本地运行，保护隐私                  ✅ 全开源，可私有化部署
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

2.3 Technical Highlights

Several Hermes modules achieve industry-leading capabilities in their respective areas:

  • Memory system: Full-session history search using SQLite FTS5, plus LLM summaries
  • Skills system: Agent-driven automatic extraction and reuse of experience
  • Context compression: Intelligent summary-based compression that preserves key information
  • Terminal backends: Six supported backends: local, Docker, SSH, Daytona, Modal, and Singularity
  • MCP integration: Connect any external tool server using Model Context Protocol

Chapter 3: System Architecture Overview

3.1 Overall Architecture

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                              用户（你）                                │
│           终端 / Telegram / Discord / WhatsApp / Signal / Email        │
└─────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────┘
                              │  各自平台协议
                              ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Hermes Gateway（消息网关）                          │
│                                                                       │
│  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌─────────────┐  ┌────────────┐ │
│  │ Telegram    │  │ Discord     │  │ Slack       │  │ Email      │ │
│  │ 适配器       │  │ 适配器       │  │ 适配器       │  │ 适配器      │ │
│  └──────┬──────┘  └──────┬──────┘  └──────┬──────┘  └─────┬──────┘ │
│         └────────────────┴────────────────┴───────────────┘         │
│                                │                                      │
│                       ┌────────▼────────┐                           │
│                       │  run.py           │                           │
│                       │  统一消息格式      │                           │
│                       │  Session 管理     │                           │
│                       │  Slash 命令路由    │                           │
│                       └────────┬────────┘                           │
└────────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────┘
                                 │  统一消息对象
                                 ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Hermes Agent Core（核心）                          │
│                                                                       │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │

│  │                                                                │ │

│                                                                       │

│  │ builder      │  │(registry.py)  │  │(SQLite + FTS5)          │  │

3.2 Data-flow Overview

用户说："帮我读 test.py 并总结内容"

        ① 消息格式统一化（Gateway 适配器）
              │
              ▼
        ② 查找/创建 Session（SQLite）
              │
              ▼
        ③ 组装系统提示词（prompt_builder）
              │  身份 + 工具列表 + 用户偏好 + 记忆上下文
              ▼
        ④ 发给 AI 模型（"用户要读文件并总结，有哪些工具可用？"）
              │
              ▼
        ⑤ AI 思考后返回 tool_call
              │  name="read_file", args={path: "test.py"}
              ▼
        ⑥ 从注册表找到 read_file handler，执行它
              │
              ▼
        ⑦ 文件内容返回给 AI 模型（结果加入 messages）
              │
              ▼
        ⑧ AI 再次思考："我读到了文件内容，现在总结它"
              │
              ▼
        ⑨ AI 返回最终总结（不再有 tool_call）
              │
              ▼
        ⑩ 回复显示给用户

Chapter 4: Core Module Design

Hermes's architecture revolves around three core questions:

问题1：工具越来越多，怎么管理？       → 注册表模式（Registry Pattern）
问题2：模型越来越多，怎么切换？       → Provider 抽象层
问题3：功能越来越多，代码怎么改？      → 插件化（Plugins）+ Skills

Chapter 5: The Tool System (Registry Pattern)

5.1 Background

  • Hermes includes 60+ tools and supports dynamic expansion through MCP
  • The tool count continues to grow without making the code chaotic
  • Tools have different dependencies: some require API keys, while others only operate on local files
  • Tools must be enabled or disabled by platform; for example, certain sensitive tools are enabled only in CLI mode

5.2 Three-layer Architecture

第1层：定义层（每个工具文件）
  tools/file_tools.py  ─┐
  tools/terminal_tool.py ─┼─ 每个文件末尾调用 registry.register()
  tools/web_tools.py    ─┘

第2层：注册中心（tools/registry.py）
  唯一真相来源：_registry[name] = ToolEntry(...)
  提供 register() / get() / dispatch() 三个接口

第3层：分发层（model_tools.py）
  handle_function_call(name, args)
  根据 name 找到 registry entry，调用 handler，返回 JSON 字符串

5.3 Tool Registration

Each tool file, such as todo_tool.py, has the following structure:

# ============ 第1步：定义 Schema（给 AI 模型看的说明书）============

TODO_SCHEMA = {
    "name": "todo",
    "description": (
        "管理任务清单。..."
    ),
    "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "todos": {
                "type": "array",
                "description": "任务列表..."
            },
            "merge": {
                "type": "boolean",
                "description": "是否合并..."
            }
        },
        "required": []
    }
}

# ============ 第2步：实现 Handler（真正做事的 Python 函数）============

def todo_tool(todos=None, merge=False, store=None):
    # ... 实际逻辑 ...
    return json.dumps({"todos": current_list})

# ============ 第3步：注册到全局注册表（末尾调用一次即可）============

registry.register(
    name="todo",                    # 工具名
    toolset="todo",                 # 属于哪个工具组
    schema=TODO_SCHEMA,              # Schema 说明书
    handler=lambda args, **kw: todo_tool(...),  # 执行函数
    check_fn=check_todo_requirements,  # 可用性检查
    emoji="📋",                      # UI 图标
)

Key Insight: Schema and Handler Are Completely Separate

  • The schema is an instruction manual for the AI model, describing the tool's name, parameters, and function
  • The handler is the executor: the actual Python logic
  • Changing the schema does not affect the handler, and vice versa

5.4 Tool Discovery

Tool loading is fully automatic and happens when model_tools.py is imported:

def _discover_tools():
    """Import all tool modules to trigger their registry.register() calls."""
    _modules = [
        "tools.todo_tool",
        "tools.file_tools",
        "tools.terminal_tool",
        "tools.web_tools",
        # ... 60+ 个模块
    ]
    for mod_name in _modules:
        importlib.import_module(mod_name)  # 导入时自动注册

_discover_tools()  # 模块加载时立即执行

Adding a tool therefore means adding a Python file and one registration line at the bottom, with zero configuration.

5.5 Toolset Grouping

Tools are grouped by function, and each group can be enabled or disabled as a whole:

toolset "file"      → read_file, write_file, patch, search_files
toolset "terminal"  → terminal, process (background process)
toolset "web"       → web_search, browser_navigate, browser_snapshot
toolset "delegate"  → delegate_task (子 Agent)
toolset "session"  → session_search (跨会话搜索)
toolset "skills"    → skill_view, skill_manage, skills_list

Users can configure groups through the hermes tools command rather than setting up each tool individually.

Chapter 6: The Messaging Gateway (Adapter Pattern)

6.1 Background

Different chat platforms use entirely different messaging protocols:

Telegram：     通过 Bot API (HTTP Long Polling)
Discord：      通过 WebSocket Gateway API
Slack：        通过 WebSocket + HTTP
WhatsApp：     通过 Baileys/Meta 官方 API
Email：        通过 IMAP/SMTP

If platform-specific handling lives directly in the core, every new platform requires risky changes to core code.

6.2 Adapter-pattern Architecture

                        统一消息格式
                         ▲
                         │ Gateway Core (run.py)
                         │
┌────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        │                                             │
│    ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐                         │
│    │                                       │                         │
│    ▼                                       ▼                         │
│  Telegram 适配器                        Discord 适配器                  │
│  platform/telegram.py                   platform/discord.py           │
│                                         │                             │
│  解析 Telegram API                      解析 Discord WebSocket         │
│  → 统一消息                             → 统一消息                     │
│                                         │                             │
│  发送：统一回复                         发送：统一回复                 │
│  → Telegram API                         → Discord API                │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Unified message format, defined by the Gateway Core:

class UnifiedMessage:
    user_id: str          # 用户唯一标识
    platform: str         # "telegram" / "discord" / ...
    text: str             # 消息文本
    attachments: list      # 图片/文件等附件
    chat_id: str          # 会话 ID
    thread_id: str | None # 话题 ID（支持 Discord thread 等）
    timestamp: datetime   # 时间戳

6.3 Why Is This Design Good?

  • Adding a platform: Write only a new adapter file, around 500–1,000 lines; the core run.py requires no changes
  • Independent evolution: Each platform adapter can be tested and upgraded independently
  • Fault isolation: A crash in one platform's adapter does not affect other platforms or the core

Chapter 7: The AI Loop (ReAct Pattern)

7.1 What Is ReAct?

ReAct = Reason + Act. This is currently the dominant design pattern for AI agents:

Reason（思考）：AI 模型分析当前情况，决定下一步做什么
Act（行动）：   AI 模型调用工具执行

交替进行，直到任务完成

7.2 Hermes's AI Loop

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     run_agent.py 核心循环                     │
│                                                             │
│  while (api_call_count < max_iterations                     │
│         AND iteration_budget.remaining > 0):                 │
│                                                             │
│      ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│      │  Step 1：发 API 请求                               │  │
│      │                                                   │  │
│      │  client.chat.completions.create(                 │  │
│      │    messages=[                                     │  │
│      │      {role:"system", content:系统提示词},         │  │
│      │      {role:"user",   content:用户输入},           │  │
│      │      {role:"assistant",content:AI上一轮回复},     │  │
│      │      ...（完整对话历史）                           │  │
│      │    ],                                             │  │
│      │    tools=[read_file_schema, web_search_schema]   │  │
│      │  )                                                │  │
│      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
│                           │                                  │
│                           ▼                                  │
│      ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────┐  │
│      │  Step 2：判断返回类型                              │  │
│      │                                                   │  │
│      │  if response.tool_calls:  # AI 要求调用工具      │  │
│      │      │                                            │  │
│      │      │  for each tool_call:                       │  │
│      │      │    result = registry.dispatch(            │  │
│      │      │      name=tool_call.name,                  │  │
│      │      │      args=tool_call.args                   │  │
│      │      │    )                                       │  │
│      │      │    messages.append({                     │  │
│      │      │      role:"tool",                          │  │
│      │      │      tool_call_id: xxx,                   │  │
│      │      │      content: result                      │  │
│      │      │    })                                      │  │
│      │      │                                            │  │
│      │      │  → 回到 Step 1，继续问 AI                  │  │
│      │      │                                            │  │
│      │  else:  # AI 不需要工具了，这是最终回复             │  │
│      │      │                                            │  │
│      │      → break 循环，返回最终回复给用户             │  │
│      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

7.3 Why Is a Loop Necessary?

Complex tasks cannot be completed in one step. For example:

用户："帮我分析 /project 目录的代码，写一份报告"

AI 第1轮思考："我需要先看看目录里有哪些文件"
  → tool_call: terminal("ls -la /project")

AI 第2轮思考："好，我看到有 main.py, utils.py, tests/ 等"
  → tool_call: read_file("main.py")
  → tool_call: read_file("utils.py")

AI 第3轮思考："文件内容读完了，我来写报告"
  → 最终回复（无 tool_call，break 出去）

7.4 Loop Control: iteration_budget

Set a maximum iteration count to prevent the AI from calling tools forever:

class IterationBudget:
    max_total = 90        # 最多 90 次 API 调用
    remaining = max_total

    def consume(self) -> bool:
        """返回 False 表示预算耗尽，强制退出"""
        if self.remaining <= 0:
            return False
        self.remaining -= 1
        return True

Scenario: If a tool returns an error, such as a network timeout, the AI may repeatedly retry it. Once the budget is exhausted, execution is forcibly stopped to prevent an infinite loop.

7.5 What If the Context Gets Too Long?

When conversation history grows close to the model's context limit, it triggers context compression:

压缩前：
messages = [系统提示词, 用户问题1, AI回答1, 用户问题2, AI回答2, ... 100轮...]

压缩后：
messages = [
    系统提示词,
    [摘要: 前50轮对话的核心信息],
    最近10轮完整对话  ← 总是保留最新的对话
]

Compression strategy (context_compressor.py):

  • Protect recent turns: Never compress the most recent N conversation turns
  • Summarize the middle: Use an LLM to summarize earlier conversation, retaining key points
  • Recount: Re-estimate tokens after compression to ensure the context remains within limits

Chapter 8: Prompt Construction (Layered Assembly)

8.1 Background

AI models are general purpose: GPT-4 and Claude do not inherently know who they are. To turn a model into Hermes, a system prompt must provide identity, capabilities, preferences, and context.

8.2 Layered Prompt Assembly

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  系统提示词（System Prompt）                    │
│                                                              │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ 第1层：基础身份层（最底层，几乎不变）                      │ │
│  │                                                        │ │
│  │ "You are Hermes, an AI assistant built by Nous Research."│ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                            +                                 │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ 第2层：能力描述层（工具定义）                              │ │
│  │                                                        │ │
│  │ "You have access to the following tools:"              │ │
│  │ "  - read_file: Read a file with pagination..."         │ │
│  │ "  - web_search: Search the web..."                     │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                            +                                 │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ 第3层：用户偏好层（来自记忆系统）                          │ │
│  │                                                        │ │
│  │ "User information:"                                     │ │
│  │ "  - Name: Eva, works at 末龙科技"                       │ │
│  │ "  - Preferred language: Python"                       │ │
│  │ "  - Dislikes: Americano coffee"                        │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                            +                                 │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ 第4层：上下文层（动态信息）                               │ │
│  │                                                        │ │
│  │ "Current working directory: /Users/eva/code/project"    │ │
│  │ "Today's date: 2025-01-15"                              │ │
│  │ "Current git branch: feature/login"                      │ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                            +                                 │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│  │ 第5层：Skills 指令（来自 Skills 系统）                   │ │
│  │                                                        │ │
│  │ "For Python debugging tasks, use the debug-python skill"│ │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

8.3 Responsibilities of prompt_builder.py

prompt_builder.py dynamically assembles these layers, deciding what to include based on the following factors:

def _build_system_prompt(self) -> str:
    layers = []

    # 第1层：基础身份
    layers.append(self._get_identity_block())

    # 第2层：工具列表（只包含当前启用的工具）
    layers.append(self._get_tools_block())

    # 第3层：用户偏好（从 memory 读取）
    if self.memory_enabled:
        layers.append(self._get_user_preferences_block())

    # 第4层：当前上下文
    layers.append(self._get_context_block())

    # 第5层：Skills 指令
    layers.append(self._get_skills_block())

    return "\n\n".join(layers)

Chapter 9: Memory and Skills

9.1 Ordinary Memory vs. Skills

普通记忆（Memory）         → 存储事实（"用户叫 Eva"）
Skills                   → 存储经验（"遇到 X 类型问题，用 Y 方法解决"）

9.2 How Memory Works

用户说："我下周三要去北京出差"

            │
            ▼ 记忆工具自动提取
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  实体提取：                                  │
│    - 用户：Eva                              │
│    - 事件：出差                              │
│    - 地点：北京                              │
│    - 时间：下周三                            │
│                                             │
│  存储到 ~/.hermes/memory/                  │
│  文件：travel_beijing_eva_2025.md           │
└──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┘
                       │
           下一轮对话开始时
                       │
                       ▼ 从 memory/ 读取相关记忆
           注入系统提示词 → AI 知道"用户要出差去北京"

9.3 How Skills Work

Skills are Hermes's most distinctive innovation. The central idea is:

"Rather than telling an agent how to work, let it learn how to work for itself."

用户让 Hermes 完成一个复杂任务
  → Hermes 执行完成
  → Hermes 问自己："我应该把这次经验记成一个 Skill 吗？"
  → 如果值得记住：
      创建 ~/.hermes/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md
      内容包括：
        - 这个 Skill 在什么场景下触发
        - 具体操作步骤
        - 注意事项和陷阱
  → 下次遇到同类任务：
      Hermes 自动检索相关 Skill → 加载步骤 → 执行

Skill storage format (Markdown):

# python-debug

## 触发条件
当用户描述了 Python 错误、异常、或要求"帮我调试"时触发。

## 操作步骤
1. 首先让用户提供完整的错误信息
2. 使用 terminal_tool 运行出错命令，获取完整 stack trace
3. 分析错误类型：
   - SyntaxError → 检查拼写和缩进
   - ImportError → 检查包是否安装、路径是否正确
   - IndexError  → 检查列表边界
4. 根据错误类型逐一排查
5. 提供修复方案和修改后的代码

## 注意事项
- 不要在看到完整错误前就猜测原因
- stack trace 从下往上看，找到第一个 ERROR 行

9.4 Retrieving and Invoking Skills

When a user describes a task, Hermes automatically:

  1. 1. Retrieves — Searches the Skills directory for relevant Skills
  2. 2. Loads — Injects the matching Skill's Markdown into the prompt
  3. 3. Executes — Follows the Skill's steps

Chapter 10: Model Abstraction (Provider Pattern)

10.1 Background

Dozens of LLM providers use different API formats and authentication methods. Hard-coding one API would require extensive code changes when switching models.

10.2 Hermes's Solution

Hermes code uses only an OpenAI-compatible format:

from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-xxx",
    base_url="https://api.anthropic.com"  # 可以指向任何兼容端点
)

# 这个调用格式，可以是：
#   - Claude（通过 Anthropic 或 OpenRouter）
#   - GPT-4（原生 OpenAI）
#   - 任何 OpenRouter 支持的 200+ 模型
#   - 本地 Ollama 模型
client.chat.completions.create(
    model="claude-3-opus",
    messages=[...],
    tools=[...]
)

10.3 Supported Model Types

ProviderFormatConfiguration
Anthropic (native)Anthropic SDKANTHROPIC_API_KEY
OpenAIOpenAI SDKOPENAI_API_KEY
OpenRouterOpenAI-compatibleOPENROUTER_API_KEY
Xiaomi MiMoOpenAI-compatibleMIMO_API_KEY
MiniMaxOpenAI-compatibleMINIMAX_API_KEY
Local OllamaOpenAI-compatibleOLLAMA_BASE_URL
Hugging FaceInference APIHF_API_KEY
Custom endpointOpenAI-compatibleAny base_url

10.4 Switching Models

Users need just one command:

/model claude-3-opus
/model gpt-4-turbo
/model openrouter:anthropic/claude-3-opus
/model ollama:llama3

model_switch.py automatically handles provider detection, API-address resolution, and credential matching, transparently to the user.

Chapter 11: What Makes the Architecture Good?

11.1 Four Dimensions for Evaluating Architecture

Maintainability: How much code must change to add a feature?

新增一个工具        → 新建 1 个 Python 文件 + 1 行注册代码
新增一个平台适配器   → 新建 1 个适配器文件
新增一个模型支持    → 改配置，不改代码
修复工具 Bug        → 只改该工具文件
核心重构            → 工具和适配器都不受影响

Testability: Can each module be tested independently?

工具函数           → ✅ 可以单独写单元测试
注册表             → ✅ 可以注册假工具后测试分发逻辑
适配器             → ✅ 可以 Mock 测试，不依赖真实 API
prompt_builder     → ✅ 可以构造不同配置测试输出

Extensibility: Can it run in more environments?

终端后端：        本地 / Docker / SSH / Daytona / Modal / Singularity
消息平台：        Telegram / Discord / Slack / WhatsApp / Signal / Email
外部扩展：        MCP（Model Context Protocol）支持任意外部工具服务器

Flexibility: Can unnecessary parts be disabled?

工具集（toolsets）  → 按组启用/禁用
平台适配器          → 配置文件开关
记忆系统            → 可关闭（节省资源）
Skills 系统         → 可关闭

11.2 Comparison with Other Agent Frameworks

DimensionLangChainAutoGenCrewAIHermes
Multiplatform access❌❌❌✅
Persistent memory⚠️ Must be built yourself❌❌✅
Self-evolving Skills❌❌❌✅
Open source✅✅✅✅
Model agnostic⚠️⚠️⚠️✅
Parallel subagents✅✅✅✅
Local deployment✅✅✅✅

Chapter 12: Popular Features Explained

12.1 Ranked by Usage Frequency

RankFeatureCode LocationWhy It Is Popular
1Terminal command executiontools/terminal_tool.pyRun commands directly in chat without switching windows
2File reading, writing, and searchtools/file_tools.pyInspect code and change files without opening an editor
3Web searchtools/web_tools.pyAsk questions and receive results directly
4Scheduled tasks (Cron)tools/cronjob_tools.py"Remind me of the meeting every day at 9"—set it once and it keeps working
5Cross-platform messaginggateway/platforms/*Send a task on WeChat and continue it in the terminal
6Parallel subagentstools/delegate_tool.py"Research three topics at once"—three agents work simultaneously
7Skill evolutiontools/skill_manager_tool.pyThe agent learns from mistakes and grows smarter
8Model switchinghermes_cli/model_switch.pyChange models with one command, without technical modifications

12.2 Most Distinctive Feature: Self-evolving Skills

This is the biggest distinction between Hermes and all other agent frameworks.

Traditional agent:

用户每次遇到同类问题 → 都要重新描述一遍 → Agent 每次重新摸索

Hermes with Skills:

第1次遇到问题 → Agent 解决 → 判断值得记住 → 存入 Skill
第2次遇到同类问题 → Agent 自动找到 Skill → 直接套用经验
第N次 → Skill 越来越完善，Agent 越来越专业

Hermes thus achieves real learning—not by updating model parameters, but by accumulating experiential knowledge.

12.3 Most Practical Feature: Multiplatform Unification

A real workflow for most users:

在地铁上（微信）     → 发一条消息给 Hermes："帮我看看代码有没有 Bug"
到公司（电脑）        → 打开终端 → 继续同一个对话，Hermes 已经记住了任务
下班路上（Telegram）  → 再发一条："帮我写个报告总结今天的发现"
回家（躺在床上）      → 语音问 Hermes："今天完成了什么？"

The entire process is continuous, with the same agent, memory system, and accumulated Skills.

Appendix: Repository Directory Structure

├── model_tools.py         ← 工具发现 + 调用分发

│   ├── prompt_builder.py  ← 系统提示词组装

title: Hermes Agent Tutorial (3): A Deep Dive into the Tool System
html:
A Deep Dive into the Hermes Tool System

Chapter goal: Understand the details of Hermes' tool-system design and add a new tool yourself
Prerequisites: The previous chapter, “System Architecture”
Documentation: https://github.com/Eva-Dengyh/AI-Fullstack-Notes

Contents

  • 1. Where the tool system fits in the architecture
  • 2. The registry pattern in detail
  • 3. Schema: An instruction manual for the AI model
  • 4. Handler: The Python function that does the work
  • 5. Discovery: How tools are found
  • 6. Tracing the complete invocation path
  • 7. Toolsets: Managing tools in groups
  • 8. Hands-on: Adding a weather-query tool to Hermes

1. Where the tool system fits in the architecture

Recall the previous chapter's overall architecture. The tool system is at the bottom:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Hermes Gateway                      │
│              (消息进 / 消息出)                    │
└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                      │
┌─────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
│              run_agent.py                        │
│         AI 循环：问模型 → 执行工具 → 问模型       │
└─────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                      │ 工具调用
┌─────────────────────┴───────────────────────────┐
│           tools/registry.py                     │
│         （工具注册中心）                          │
│         tools/file_tools.py                     │
│         tools/terminal_tool.py                  │
│         tools/web_tools.py                      │
│         tools/delegate_tool.py                  │
│         ...（60+ 工具）                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

In one sentence: the tool system is Hermes' hands—all interactions with the outside world, including reading files, searching the web, and executing commands, happen through tools.

2. The registry pattern in detail

2.1 What is the registry pattern?

An everyday analogy: It resembles a company's front-desk register. Each new employee fills in their own entry: “My name is XX, my desk is YY, and I can do ZZ.” Visitors consult the register to find someone without knowing where they live or what they like.

The code analogy:

# 传统方式（耦合）：
class FileTools:
    def read_file(self, path): ...
    def write_file(self, path, content): ...

class TerminalTools:
    def run_command(self, cmd): ...

# 每加一个工具 → 改一次类的定义 → 核心代码越来越臃肿

# 注册表方式（解耦）：
registry = ToolRegistry()

def read_file_handler(args): 
    return read_file(args["path"])

registry.register(
    name="read_file",
    schema={...},      # 给 AI 看的说明
    handler=read_file_handler  # 真正做事的函数
)

# 新增工具？完全不需要动 registry.py
# 只需要在工具文件里加一行 registry.register(...)

2.2 ToolRegistry's data structure

class ToolRegistry:
    def __init__(self):
        self._tools: Dict[str, ToolEntry] = {}
        # 注册表本体：名字 → 工具条目

    def register(self, name, schema, handler, ...):
        entry = ToolEntry(name, schema, handler, ...)
        self._tools[name] = entry  # 注册动作

    def get(self, name) -> ToolEntry:
        return self._tools.get(name)  # 查询动作

    def dispatch(self, name, args) -> str:
        entry = self.get(name)
        return entry.handler(args)  # 执行动作

2.3 Why not class inheritance?

With traditional object-oriented design, tools would form an inheritance tree like this:

Tool
├── FileTool
│   ├── ReadFileTool
│   ├── WriteFileTool
│   └── SearchFilesTool
├── TerminalTool
│   ├── RunCommandTool
│   └── BackgroundProcessTool
└── WebTool
    ├── SearchTool
    └── BrowserTool

Problems:

  • Python does not support multiple inheritance, but tools often need several capabilities simultaneously, such as both reading/writing files and executing commands
  • Adding a tool requires changing the class hierarchy
  • Testing is complex because every subclass must be instantiated

Advantages of the registry pattern:

  • Tools are independent, without a hierarchy
  • A new tool requires only a new file and one registration line
  • Tests can target individual tools without constructing an inheritance tree

3. Schema: An instruction manual for the AI model

3.1 What is a schema?

A schema is a JSON object describing:

工具叫什么名字
接受哪些参数（名字、类型、含义）
工具是做什么的
返回什么格式

It is a tool manual for the AI model, rather than for humans.

3.2 Schema structure

Take the read_file tool as an example:

{
  "name": "read_file",
  "description": "Read a text file with pagination and line numbers.\n\n"
                "Use this instead of cat/head/tail in terminal.\n\n"
                "Output format: 'LINE_NUM|CONTENT'.\n\n"
                "Args:\n"
                "  path (str): Path to the file (absolute, relative, or ~/path)\n"
                "  offset (int): Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)\n"
                "  limit (int): Maximum lines to read (default 500, max 2000)\n\n"
                "Returns:\n"
                "  dict with 'content', 'total_lines', 'is_binary', 'is_image'",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "path": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "Path to the file to read (absolute, relative, or ~/path)"
      },
      "offset": {
        "type": "integer",
        "description": "Line number to start reading from (1-indexed, default: 1)",
        "default": 1
      },
      "limit": {
        "type": "integer", 
        "description": "Maximum number of lines to read (default: 500, max: 2000)",
        "default": 500
      }
    },
    "required": ["path"]
  }
}

3.3 How does the AI model use a schema?

AI 模型看到 Schema 后：

"好的，我有一个叫 read_file 的工具。
 它接受一个叫 path 的字符串参数（必填），
 还有 offset 和 limit 两个可选整数参数。
 当用户让我'看看某个文件内容'时，我就知道要调用它。"

这是 LLM 的 function calling 能力——模型根据对话上下文，
自动决定调用哪个工具、传什么参数。

3.4 Best practices for writing schemas

A good schema:

  • Describes parameters clearly, including when each should be used
  • States default values when present
  • Uses descriptions to explain usage scenarios, beyond parameter meanings

A poor schema:

{
  "name": "weather",
  "description": "Get weather",
  "parameters": {
    "properties": {"city": {"type": "string"}}
  }
}

A good schema:

{
  "name": "weather",
  "description": "Get current weather and forecast for a city.\n\n"
                "Use when: user asks about weather, temperature, rain, etc.\n\n"
                "Returns: temperature, conditions, humidity, forecast.",
  "parameters": {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "city": {
        "type": "string",
        "description": "City name (e.g. 'Beijing', 'Tokyo')"
      },
      "forecast_days": {
        "type": "integer", 
        "description": "Number of days to forecast (1-7, default: 3)",
        "default": 3
      }
    },
    "required": ["city"]
  }
}

4. Handler: The Python function that does the work

4.1 A handler's responsibilities

A handler is a plain Python function responsible for:

  1. 1. Receiving arguments as a dictionary
  2. 2. Performing the actual operation
  3. 3. Returning a JSON string (all tools must return JSON strings)

4.2 Standard handler signature

def my_handler(args: dict, **kwargs) -> str:
    """
    Args:
        args: 工具调用时传递的参数（字典）
        **kwargs: 额外上下文
            task_id: str      # 终端/浏览器会话隔离 ID
            session_id: str   # 会话 ID
            tool_call_id: str # 工具调用 ID（用于 trace）
    
    Returns:
        str: JSON 字符串（必须能 json.loads）
    """
    # 解析参数
    param1 = args.get("param1", "default")
    param2 = args.get("param2", 0)
    
    try:
        # 做实际的事
        result = do_something(param1, param2)
        
        # 返回 JSON 字符串
        return json.dumps({"success": True, "result": result})
    
    except Exception as e:
        # 错误也要返回 JSON 字符串
        return json.dumps({"error": f"Failed: {str(e)}"})

4.3 Why return a JSON string?

Because this return value is eventually inserted into the AI model's conversation history:

# AI 模型看到工具执行结果后，继续思考下一步

messages = [
    {"role": "user", "content": "帮我读 test.py"},
    {"role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [{"name": "read_file", "args": {"path": "test.py"}}]},
    {"role": "tool", "content": '{"content": "...file contents...", "total_lines": 50}'},
    #                                                      ↑
    #                                           必须是字符串，因为 role: tool 的
    #                                           content 字段在 API 规范里是字符串
]

4.4 A real handler example

Here is the implementation of todo_tool (tools/todo_tool.py):

class TodoStore:
    """内存中的任务清单，一个 AIAgent 实例对应一个。"""
    def __init__(self):
        self._items: List[Dict[str, str]] = []

    def write(self, todos: List[Dict], merge: bool = False) -> List[Dict]:
        if not merge:
            # 全量替换模式
            self._items = [self._validate(t) for t in self._dedupe(todos)]
        else:
            # 合并模式：按 id 更新已有项，追加新项
            existing = {item["id"]: item for item in self._items}
            for t in todos:
                item_id = t.get("id", "").strip()
                if item_id in existing:
                    # 更新字段
                    if "content" in t: existing[item_id]["content"] = t["content"]
                    if "status" in t: existing[item_id]["status"] = t["status"]
                else:
                    # 追加新项
                    self._items.append(self._validate(t))
        return self.read()  # 总是返回完整列表


def todo_tool(todos=None, merge=False, store=None) -> str:
    """
    Args:
        todos: 任务列表 [{id, content, status}]
        merge: 是否合并（True=更新已有，False=全量替换）
        store: TodoStore 实例（从 AIAgent 注入）
    """
    if todos is None:
        # 读模式：没有 todos 参数
        return json.dumps({"todos": store.read()})
    
    # 写模式
    result = store.write(todos, merge=merge)
    return json.dumps({"todos": result})

5. Discovery: How tools are found

5.1 Introducing the problem

With over 60 tools, manually importing every file at startup would be verbose:

# ❌ 错误方式：维护一个巨大的 import 列表
import tools.todo_tool
import tools.file_tools
import tools.terminal_tool
import tools.web_tools
# ... 60 行...

# 如果要加一个新工具，要改这个列表

5.2 Hermes' solution: Automatic discovery

model_tools.py dynamically imports every tool during module loading through importlib:

def _discover_tools():
    """
    导入所有工具模块。
    每个模块在 import 时，末尾的 registry.register() 自动执行。
    这样新增工具只需要新增文件，不需要改这个列表。
    """
    _modules = [
        "tools.ansi_strip",
        "tools.binary_extensions",
        "tools.browser_camofox",
        "tools.browser_tool",
        "tools.budget_config",
        "tools.checkpoint_manager",
        "tools.clarify_tool",
        "tools.code_execution_tool",
        "tools.credential_files",
        "tools.cronjob_tools",
        "tools.debug_helpers",
        "tools.delegate_tool",
        "tools.env_passthrough",
        "tools.file_operations",
        "tools.file_tools",
        "tools.fuzzy_match",
        "tools.homeassistant_tool",
        "tools.image_generation_tool",
        "tools.interrupt",
        "tools.managed_tool_gateway",
        "tools.mcp_oauth",
        "tools.mcp_tool",
        "tools.memory_tool",
        "tools.mixture_of_agents_tool",
        "tools.neutts_synth",
        # ... 60+ 个 ...
    ]
    
    for mod_name in _modules:
        try:
            importlib.import_module(mod_name)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("Could not import tool module %s: %s", mod_name, e)

# 模块被加载时自动执行注册
_discover_tools()

5.3 Automatic registration during module loading

Take file_tools.py as an example. At the end of the file:

# ========== 文件末尾 ==========

registry.register(
    name="read_file",
    toolset="file",
    schema=READ_FILE_SCHEMA,
    handler=_handle_read_file,
    check_fn=_check_file_reqs,
    emoji="📖",
    max_result_size_chars=float('inf')  # 不限制返回大小
)

registry.register(
    name="write_file",
    toolset="file",
    schema=WRITE_FILE_SCHEMA,
    handler=_handle_write_file,
    check_fn=_check_file_reqs,
    emoji="✍️",
    max_result_size_chars=100_000
)

registry.register(name="patch", ...)
registry.register(name="search_files", ...)

When importlib.import_module("tools.file_tools") executes, Python runs the file from beginning to end. The final registry.register() registers the tool.

5.4 The complete process for adding a tool

Adding a tool requires just two things:

# 第1步：在 tools/ 目录下新建文件，比如 tools/weather_tool.py

# 第2步：在 _discover_tools() 的列表里加一行（或者某些情况下完全不用加）
# 不，等一下——实际上只需要做第一步就够了
# 因为 model_tools.py 已经硬编码了这个列表
# 所以严格来说是：新增文件 + 修改 _modules 列表

6. Tracing the complete invocation path

6.1 The full path from user input to tool execution

用户："帮我读取 test.py"

        │
        ▼ ① Gateway 适配器解析用户消息
           unified_message = {user_id, text: "帮我读取 test.py", ...}
        │
        ▼ ② run_agent.run_conversation()
           把消息加入 messages[]
        │
        ▼ ③ 组装系统提示词（prompt_builder）
        │
        ▼ ④ 发 API 给 AI 模型
           client.chat.completions.create(
               messages=[系统提示词, 用户消息],
               tools=[read_file schema, write_file schema, ...]
           )
        │
        ▼ ⑤ AI 模型思考，决定调用 read_file
           response.tool_calls = [
               {"name": "read_file", "args": {"path": "test.py", "offset": 1, "limit": 500}}
           ]
        │
        ▼ ⑥ 主循环发现 tool_calls，执行工具
           from model_tools import handle_function_call
           │
           ▼ ⑦ handle_function_call 路由
              │
              ▼ ⑧ registry.dispatch("read_file", args)
                 │
                 ▼ ⑨ 找到 read_file 的 ToolEntry
                    entry = registry._tools["read_file"]
                    │
                    ▼ ⑩ 调用 handler
                       result = entry.handler(args)
                       # 内部执行 open("test.py").read()
                       # 返回 json.dumps({"content": "...", "total_lines": 50})
                    │
                    ▼ ⑪ 把结果加回 messages[]
                    messages.append({
                        "role": "tool",
                        "tool_call_id": "xxx",
                        "content": '{"content": "...", "total_lines": 50}'
                    })
                 │
                 ▼ ⑫ 回到循环开头，再次发 API 给模型
                    "用户要我读文件，我已经读完了，这是内容：..."
        │
        ▼ ⑬ AI 模型看到文件内容，组织语言回复用户
           最终回复（无 tool_calls）→ break 循环
        │
        ▼ ⑭ Gateway 把回复发回给用户

6.2 What does handle_function_call do?

# model_tools.py

def handle_function_call(
    function_name: str,
    function_args: Dict[str, Any],
    task_id: Optional[str] = None,
    tool_call_id: Optional[str] = None,
    session_id: Optional[str] = None,
    user_task: Optional[str] = None,
    enabled_tools: Optional[List[str]] = None,
    skip_pre_tool_call_hook: bool = False,
) -> str:
    """
    工具调用的分发入口。
    所有工具调用都经过这里。
    """
    # 第1步：类型强制转换（"42" → 42, "true" → True）
    function_args = coerce_tool_args(function_name, function_args)
    
    # 第2步：插件钩子（pre_tool_call）
    # 允许插件在工具执行前拦截或阻止
    if not skip_pre_tool_call_hook:
        block_message = get_pre_tool_call_block_message(...)
        if block_message is not None:
            return json.dumps({"error": block_message})
    
    # 第3步：执行工具
    if function_name == "execute_code":
        # execute_code 比较特殊，需要传入 enabled_tools
        result = registry.dispatch(
            "execute_code", function_args,
            task_id=task_id,
            enabled_tools=enabled_tools
        )
    else:
        result = registry.dispatch(
            function_name, function_args,
            task_id=task_id,
            user_task=user_task
        )
    
    # 第4步：插件钩子（post_tool_call）
    invoke_hook("post_tool_call", tool_name=function_name, ...)
    
    return result

6.3 What does registry.dispatch do?

# tools/registry.py

class ToolRegistry:
    def dispatch(self, name: str, args: dict, **kwargs) -> str:
        """根据名字找到工具，执行它，返回 JSON 字符串。"""
        
        # 第1步：找到工具条目
        entry = self.get_entry(name)
        if not entry:
            return json.dumps({"error": f"Unknown tool: {name}"})
        
        # 第2步：调用 handler
        try:
            if entry.is_async:
                # 异步工具（使用了 async def 的工具）
                from model_tools import _run_async
                return _run_async(entry.handler(args, **kwargs))
            return entry.handler(args, **kwargs)
        
        # 第3步：异常处理
        except Exception as e:
            logger.exception("Tool %s dispatch error: %s", name, e)
            return json.dumps({
                "error": f"Tool execution failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
            })

7. Toolsets: Managing tools in groups

7.1 Why are toolsets needed?

With over 60 tools, disabling all file-operation tools would otherwise require configuring each individually:

# ❌ 没有工具集时：
disabled_tools = ["read_file", "write_file", "patch", "search_files", ...]

With a toolset, one configuration line is enough:

# ✅ 有工具集时：
disabled_toolsets = ["file"]  # 关闭整个 file 工具组

7.2 Toolset definitions (toolsets.py)

# toolsets.py

_HERMES_CORE_TOOLS = [
    # file 工具集：文件操作
    "tools.file_tools",
    
    # terminal 工具集：命令执行
    "tools.terminal_tool",
    
    # delegate 工具集：子 Agent
    "tools.delegate_tool",
    
    # session 工具集：会话搜索
    "tools.session_search_tool",
    
    # ... 更多核心工具
]

_OPTIONAL_TOOLS = {
    "web": [
        "tools.web_tools",
        "tools.browser_tool",
    ],
    "image_gen": [
        "tools.image_generation_tool",
        "tools.tts_tool",
        "tools.transcription_tools",
    ],
    "cronjob": [
        "tools.cronjob_tools",
    ],
    "skills": [
        "tools.skill_manager_tool",
        "tools.skills_sync",
        "tools.skills_tool",
    ],
    "mcp": [
        "tools.mcp_tool",
    ],
}

7.3 Toolset availability checks

Each tool can declare a check_fn (availability-check function):

def _check_file_reqs() -> bool:
    """文件工具：始终可用（纯本地操作）"""
    return True

def _check_browser_reqs() -> bool:
    """浏览器工具：需要 BROWSERBASE_API_KEY"""
    import os
    return bool(os.getenv("BROWSERBASE_API_KEY"))

registry.register(
    name="browser_navigate",
    toolset="browser",
    schema=BROWSER_NAVIGATE_SCHEMA,
    handler=browser_navigate,
    check_fn=_check_browser_reqs,  # 没有 API Key 时自动不可用
    requires_env=["BROWSERBASE_API_KEY"],
)

8. Hands-on: Adding a weather-query tool to Hermes

8.1 Goal

Create a weather tool:

  • Input: City name as a string
  • Output: Weather information—temperature, humidity, and conditions
  • Calls an external weather API

8.2 Step 1: Create the tool file

# tools/weather_tool.py

import json
import os
import urllib.request
from typing import Dict, Any

# ============================================================
# Schema：给 AI 模型看的说明书
# ============================================================

WEATHER_SCHEMA = {
    "name": "weather",
    "description": (
        "Get current weather and forecast for a city.\n\n"
        "Use when: user asks about weather, temperature, rain, whether to bring an umbrella, etc.\n\n"
        "Returns: temperature (°C), conditions, humidity (%), wind speed, and forecast for 3 days.\n\n"
        "Note: Weather data from wttr.in (no API key required)."
    ),
    "parameters": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
            "city": {
                "type": "string",
                "description": (
                    "City name or location. "
                    "Examples: 'Beijing', 'Tokyo', 'New York', 'London UK', 'Tokyo JP'"
                )
            }
        },
        "required": ["city"]
    }
}

# ============================================================
# Handler：真正做事的函数
# ============================================================

def check_weather_requirements() -> bool:
    """weather 工具不需要 API key，wttr.in 是免费服务"""
    return True

def weather_tool(city: str, task_id: str = "default") -> str:
    """
    获取城市天气信息。
    
    Args:
        city: 城市名
        task_id: 任务 ID（用于缓存等）
    
    Returns:
        JSON 字符串，包含天气信息
    """
    if not city or not city.strip():
        return json.dumps({"error": "City name is required"})
    
    city = city.strip()
    
    try:
        # wttr.in 是一个免费的天气预报服务，不需要 API key
        # 格式：JSON
        url = f"https://wttr.in/{city}?format=j1"
        
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            url,
            headers={"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 Hermes-Agent"}
        )
        
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10) as response:
            data = json.loads(response.read().decode("utf-8"))
        
        # 解析 wttr.in 的返回格式
        current = data["current_condition"][0]
        nearest_area = data["nearest_area"][0]
        
        result = {
            "city": nearest_area.get("areaName", [{}])[0].get("value", city),
            "country": nearest_area.get("country", [{}])[0].get("value", ""),
            "temperature_c": current["temp_C"],
            "feels_like_c": current["FeelsLikeC"],
            "humidity": current["humidity"],
            "weather": current["weatherDesc", [{}])[0].get("value", ""),
            "wind_speed_kmh": current["windspeedKmph"],
            "wind_dir": current["winddir16Point"],
            "uv_index": current["uvIndex"],
            "forecast": []
        }
        
        # 解析 3 天预报
        for day in data["weather"]:
            result["forecast"].append({
                "date": day["date"],
                "max_temp_c": day["maxtempC"],
                "min_temp_c": day["mintempC"],
                "avg_temp_c": day["avgtempC"],
                "condition": day["hourly"][4]["weatherDesc"][0]["value"],
            })
        
        return json.dumps({
            "success": True,
            "data": result
        })
    
    except urllib.error.URLError as e:
        return json.dumps({
            "error": f"Failed to fetch weather for '{city}': network error. "
                     f"Please check the city name and try again."
        })
    except Exception as e:
        return json.dumps({
            "error": f"Failed to fetch weather: {str(e)}"
        })

# ============================================================
# 注册到全局注册表
# ============================================================

from tools.registry import registry

registry.register(
    name="weather",
    toolset="web",          # 天气属于 web 工具集（依赖网络）
    schema=WEATHER_SCHEMA,
    handler=lambda args, **kw: weather_tool(
        city=args.get("city", ""),
        task_id=kw.get("task_id", "default")
    ),
    check_fn=check_weather_requirements,
    emoji="🌤️",
)

8.3 Step 2: Register it in the discovery list

In model_tools.py, within the _discover_tools() function, find the _modules list and add:

_modules = [
    # ... 现有模块 ...
    "tools.weather_tool",  # ← 添加这一行
]

8.4 Step 3: Verify

# 重启 Hermes（或在新会话中）

# 问 Hermes：
# "北京今天天气怎么样？"

# Hermes 会自动调用 weather 工具：
# tool_call: weather(city="北京")
# 
# 工具返回：
# {"success": true, "data": {"city": "Beijing", "temperature_c": "12", ...}}
# 
# Hermes 把结果组织成自然语言回复你：
# "北京今天气温12°C，湿度45%，天气晴朗，适合外出..."

8.5 Reviewing the complete invocation path

用户问天气
    │
    ▼ AI 模型决定调用 weather(city="北京")
    │
    ▼ model_tools.handle_function_call("weather", {"city": "北京"})
    │
    ▼ registry.dispatch("weather", args)
    │
    ▼ weather_tool(city="北京")
         │
         ▼ urllib.request.urlopen("https://wttr.in/北京?format=j1")
         │
         ▼ 解析 JSON 返回
         │
         ▼ json.dumps({"success": true, "data": {...}})
    │
    ▼ 结果回到 AI 模型
    │
    ▼ AI 组织自然语言回复用户

Summary

After this chapter, you should understand:

  • Where the tool system fits in Hermes' architecture
  • The registry pattern's advantages over class inheritance
  • Schema structure and how the AI model uses it
  • Standard handler signatures and return-value conventions
  • Automatic tool discovery
  • The full invocation path from user input to tool execution
  • Why tools are grouped into toolsets
  • How to add a new Hermes tool through a complete practical example
